name: Prefix-$k$ Littlestone Dimension of Singletons
proof: For $n=1$, the class has one concept and cannot shatter a tree of positive depth. For $n\ge2$, any coordinate has both labels, so a depth-one tree satisfies the prefix constraint for every allowed $k$. At any root, the positive branch has just one concept and cannot split again, ruling out a complete tree of depth two even without the prefix constraint. Thus the value is one.
references: Database-defined variant; the comparison $\mathrm{PL}_k\leq\mathrm L$ is Proposition \ref{prop:prefix-littlestone-order} in the survey
